text:
aisha-cs: FYI customer hit a weird reconnect race where a streaming completion was delivered twice after a reconnect — partial then full, charged twice. They call it "double-final". Happens on v1 streaming endpoint when their client reconnects right as the final chunk is flushing. attaching repro steps and logs below.

kevin-support: customer provided request id: rid_7890 and session id: opaque123. billing csv shows two generation entries for same user/time. they say client reconnect sequence: open -> partial message -> connection drops -> reconnect -> full message duplicated.

kevin-support: sample minimal repro they used (curl):
```
curl -N \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: client-xyz-1" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-open'
```
They then kill the connection just after they get `event: chunk` with `seq=5` and immediately reopen using same `session_id`/resume token.

kevin-support: sample SSE snippet from their capture (obfuscated):
```
event: chunk
data: {"session":"opaque123","seq":5,"text":"...final par"}

// connection drops here (RST)

# on reconnect
event: resume
data: {"session":"opaque123","resume_seq":5}
event: chunk
data: {"session":"opaque123","seq":6,"text":"...final part continued"}
```
aisha-cs: customer claims billing shows two separate generation records for rid_7890 separated by ~1s. they want assurance they won't be billed twice and want a repro path we can run.

Tom-eng: I can repro locally, thanks for the clear snippet. Quick hypothesis: there's a small window where final flush gets emitted but session state isn't atomically marked as FINISHED in our DB. If client reconnects with resume token during that window, runtime will attempt to replay remaining tokens and the generation end gets emitted again. Looks like a race on session.mark_finished.

Tom-eng: searching logs for `session=opaque123` shows this pattern:
```
INFO runtime: start session=opaque123 request=rid_7890
DEBUG kv: persist session_state=IN_PROGRESS session=opaque123
WARN runtime: final_flush_sent session=opaque123 flush_id=fl_550
DEBUG kv: persist session_state=FINISHED session=opaque123
INFO billing: generation_record_created rid_7890 gen_id=g_901
```
But sometimes the `final_flush_sent` log appears before the `persist session_state=FINISHED` line due to async write ordering. If a reconnect arrives after `final_flush_sent` but before `persist session_state=FINISHED`, resume logic may still be allowed.

sasha-runtime: confirming — runtime uses an async background commit for session state to avoid blocking token flush. That was an optimization but this is the kind of edge-case it introduces. We also don't currently attach a strict idempotency key across stream resume operations. Currently `Idempotency-Key` is used for request-level billing but resume uses `resume_token` and `session_id` and trusts state.

liam-sre: also consider LB retries: if the client saw a RST and retried quickly, our front proxy may have retried the POST to upstream and caused duplicated upstream work. Does the customer use a single TCP connection or do they have a proxy that might reissue requests?

kevin-support: customer says they do reconnect from the client directly (no transparent proxy), i.e., they reopen a new SSE after TCP RST. they can share network pcap if needed.

Tom-eng: immediate mitigation we can recommend to customer: 1) add a short backoff (2000ms) before reconnect attempts to let server commit session state, or 2) generate a fresh `Idempotency-Key` per new stream instead of reusing the same one for resume (so billing dedupe will treat reconnect as separate and not double-charge the original generation). Not ideal but reduces duplicates.

Tom-eng: longer-term fix: make `final_flush` atomic with session commit (persist FINISHED synchronously) or mark a `final_flush_ack` token that disallows resume once emitted. Also add a server-side idempotency guard keyed on `session_id+final_flush_id` so subsequent resumes are no-ops with `204` or explicit `event: already_finalized`.

sasha-runtime: agreed. I'll open a PR to change the final commit path to synchronous commit for the final chunk path and add an explicit `final_ack` marker. Also adding extra logging: `final_ack_time` and `resume_rejected=true`.

bot-deploy: Incident created: INC-2026-134 with labels [streaming, race-condition, billing]. Assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

liam-sre: quick grep command for ops to find affected windows: `rg "final_flush_sent|persist session_state=FINISHED" /var/log/redwood/runtime/* | sed -n 'F;N;N'` — correlate with request id `rid_7890`.

aisha-cs: I'm sending the repro guidance and the temporary workaround to the customer, asking for pcap and a precise sequence. tagging @sasha-runtime and @tom-eng for the followup. :thumbsup:

kevin-support: customer asked about refund — can billing confirm we can dedupe those two generation rows if they share same `session_id` and happened within 5s? I'll open a billing ticket.

Tom-eng: yes let's coordinate with billing. For now mark this as actionable and ETA for a patch is ~48-72h depending on approval. I'll drop a follow-up in this thread when PR is up.

sasha-runtime: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/2385 — implements synchronous final commit and emits `event: final_ack`. rolling to canary after tests.

aisha-cs: thanks everyone — I'll keep the customer updated and paste the canary link once it's live.
